intro: The wider family, the new kinds of family, and the vocabulary of inheritance.
p.el pariente.nota: False friend: parents are los padres.
b1.texto:
**By marriage.** Your spouse's family is **la familia política**: **el suegro** and **la suegra**, **el cuñado** and **la cuñada**. Your child's spouse is **el yerno** or **la nuera**. In formal language a husband or wife is **el cónyuge**.

**Up and down.** **El bisabuelo**, **el tatarabuelo**; **el bisnieto**. **Los gemelos** are identical twins, **los mellizos** are not, and three babies are **trillizos**.

**Close or distant.** **Un pariente cercano**, **un pariente lejano**, **un primo segundo**. Careful: **parientes** are relatives. Parents are **padres**.

**Kinds of family.** **Una familia numerosa** has three or more children. **Una familia monoparental** has one parent. **Un hijo adoptivo**, **los padres adoptivos**, **una familia de acogida** (a foster family). A child who loses his parents **se queda huérfano**.

**Bringing up.** **Criar** a un hijo, **educar**, **crecer**. **Me crie** con mis abuelos. **Es de familia humilde.**

**Getting on.** **Llevarse bien**, **reñir**, **pelearse**, **hacer las paces**. **Es como de la familia.**

**Inheritance.** **Hacer testamento**, **heredar** una casa, **repartir la herencia**, **el heredero**. Heredar is also used for features: **ha heredado los ojos de su madre**.
b2.f0: When my great-grandmother died, who had been widowed very young, she left a house in the village and no will.
b2.f1: She had brought up five children on her own, as well as an orphaned nephew whom she always treated as one of them.
b2.f2: There were so many heirs, counting children, sons-in-law, daughters-in-law and grandchildren, that nobody knew whose each room was.
b2.f3: For years the siblings quarrelled over the inheritance and some stopped speaking to each other.
b2.f4: It was my sister-in-law, who is not a blood relative, who suggested doing up the house between all of us.
b2.f5: Since then each branch of the family has used it for a few weeks a year.
b2.f6: In August more than forty relatives get together, close and distant, and there are twins I still mix up.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, why did the siblings quarrel?
b4.o1.refuerzo: He was treated as one of them.
b4.o2.refuerzo: The text does not say that.
b5.pregunta: According to the text, who found the solution?
b5.o0.refuerzo: Fue mi cuñada quien propuso arreglar la casa.
b7.pregunta: Tengo muchos parientes en Argentina means…
b7.o2.refuerzo: Partners would be socios or parejas.
b8.pregunta: Complete: she has inherited her mother's eyes.
b9.o0: I was brought up by my grandparents.
b9.o1: I created it with my grandparents.
b9.o1.explicacion: Criarse: to grow up, to be brought up.
b10.traduccion: He is a distant relative of my mother's.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write the history of your family over three generations, including marriages, in-laws and inheritances.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Give your opinion aloud: is it true that family relationships are harder now than in the past?
